result.title: Reframing Object-Centric Reinforcement Learning: From Absolute to Relative Representations
result.comment: 13 pages, 7 figures, 10 pages Appendix, First two authors contributed equally
result.summary: Object-centric reinforcement learning agents typically receive each object's position in a fixed global frame, even though their decisions usually depend on where objects are relative to one another. These absolute views often fail to capture the local context that is most relevant to the agent's behavior. As a result, an agent must relearn the same response at every location where a configuration can occur, and its performance collapses when the scene is merely shifted. In this work, we propose a shift toward Object-Relative Coordinates fixed to Anchor (ORCA), where entities are described in a relative frame of reference. To operationalize this idea, we introduce Object-Relative inductive-Bias Transformers (ORBiT), a transformer-based architecture for processing anchor-relative inputs in reinforcement learning. Our results suggest these relative representations improve performance for both MLP and transformer agents. Furthermore, we demonstrate that ORBiT outperforms the pixel-based PPO baseline, achieving an aggregate HNS IQM greater than 1.0 over 13 Atari games. ORBiT learns the game of Foosball from scratch, dominating all baselines. In our controlled Tag environment, we further show that ORCA extends to rotations, that ORBiT generalizes to unseen numbers of distractors, and that these gains require a decision-relevant anchor.

AI.brief_summary: 论文主张在物体中心强化学习中用锚点固定的相对坐标（ORCA）取代全局绝对位置，并提出 ORBiT——以 transformer 处理锚点相对输入的架构，在 Atari 与受控 Tag 环境中验证相对表示对 MLP/transformer 智能体及平移、旋转、干扰物数量泛化的作用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「相对坐标系 + 实体 token 编码」的思路可供核查：可能为 VLM 推理中实体关系与几何信息如何写入 latent 状态、以及位置偏移下的表示稳定性提供借鉴，但原文属 RL 而非视觉推理，有效性待验证。
